<reason>CON won by capturing PRO's own examples in the opening (superbloom, Maya Bay, Hallstatt, Gion all resolved by physical management, not pin policing) and PRO never reclaimed them. CON's dilemma — either the motion binds third parties (vague, discriminatory, still leaky) or only the destination's own feeds (prevents none of the cited harms) — was the sharpest live pressure, and PRO's answer ("the motion doesn't specify the instrument," Jackson Hole as a voluntary campaign) widened the motion into anything-counts rather than defending the influencer-targeting reading. PRO's strongest material was the upstream-recruitment vs downstream-arrival framing and the aggregation mechanism, and CON's concession that aggregation is "real" gave PRO a genuine closing hook. But CON weighed it as marginal, answered the surprise-spike question credibly (fast physical controls; prediction problem symmetric), and kept a clean decision rule: "recruitment is not arrival; fragility is a capacity problem." Both sides had one clipped turn. Competitive, but CON made the debate easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 1 [B2.2–B2.3]: turning Jackson Hole into a voluntary-nudge example against PRO's mandate, and answering "some capacities are fixed" with "that is exactly why you ration access" — reframing PRO's strongest point into support for gates over pins.</best_rebuttal>
